---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

## Start with the boundary

When a workflow fails, first classify the failure as input, object/layer, dependency, method, resource, or interpretation. Do not patch an error by changing several scientific decisions at once.

## Common symptoms

### “No requested features are present”

Check the active assay, layer, feature names, and whether normalization or variable-feature selection was performed. A function can be installed and still receive the wrong object state.

### Every cell is filtered

Inspect the actual count and feature distributions before selecting thresholds. Tiny synthetic fixtures often need deliberately permissive thresholds for a software smoke test; those thresholds are not study recommendations.

### A reduction or graph is missing

Check the order of operations and the dimensions supplied. A reduction is not created merely because the package is loaded.

### A spatial function returns no result

Confirm coordinate columns, coordinate space, assay layer, and minimum spot count. Then check whether the selected backend is installed. Missing optional backends should be reported explicitly.

### The plot looks convincing but the claim is weak

Return to the sampling unit, replication, design, and evidence boundary. A clean visualization is not a substitute for a supported estimand.

## Reproduce before escalating

Save the smallest input, the exact error text, `sessionInfo()`, `packageVersion("scop")`, and the function call. Remove local paths and private identifiers before sharing.

## Reference

Use the [upstream function reference](https://mengxu98.github.io/scop/reference/) for signatures, then return here for workflow interpretation and recovery.
